extracted.intended_audience: artists, critics, and educated readers seeking criteria for evaluating or producing art
extracted.subtask_description: A prescriptive rubric for judging and creating 'true' art: art that transmits feelings uniting humanity and serves moral/religious perception rather than exclusivity, sensuality, or commercial gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as interchange of feelings
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is an organ by which man interchanges feelings with all men of past, present, and future; its function is to transmit feelings between people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works by their capacity to transmit genuine feelings across time and social boundaries; art that fails to communicate feeling is deficient. (Original formulation: 'By words man interchanges thoughts, by the forms of art he interchanges feelings.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Art must unite mankind (religious perception)
rubrics_metrics.description: True art transmits feelings that draw men together in brotherly union and embody the highest religious perception of the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer works that promote brotherhood and unity; works transmitting feelings that divide or exclude (exclusive class-feelings, patriotic intoxication, ecclesiastical superstition) are to be judged harmful. Examples of desirable artists: Dickens, Hugo, Dostoievsky; painters: Millet, Bastien-Lepage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification: art as 'real, important, necessary spiritual food'
rubrics_metrics.description: Only on the basis of verification can we select from what claims to be art those works which form 'real, important, necessary spiritual food' and separate them from harmful, useless, or counterfeit art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require a test or verification of a work's spiritual/nourishing value before endorsing it; this is the basis for distinguishing good art from harmful or trivial productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to be infected (audience effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art should be judged by the audience's capacity to be infected by it—good art infects people with high, unifying feelings; perverted art deprives people of this capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the work by whether it cultivates or destroys the audience's susceptibility to higher feelings; note societal loss when masses are 'deprived of the possibility of experiencing the highest feelings.'

rubrics_metrics.name: True art arises from an inner need
rubrics_metrics.description: A real work of art arises occasionally in the soul of an artist as the fruit of the life he has lived—produced by an inner need to express an accumulated feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value authenticity of origin: works motivated by a genuine inner necessity are true art. Contrast with works produced for other motives (see counterfeit art).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterfeit art vs true art (motive and form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeit art is produced by artisans and handicraftsmen for gain, continuously and ornamentally; it must be decked out and is designed to amuse, corrupt, or merely please rather than to transmit genuine feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for signs of production-for-pay, excessive ornamentation, simulation of art, and cultivation of public applause. These are anti-patterns indicating counterfeit art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter: universality not exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Art of the future will not transmit feelings accessible only to members of the rich or a section of people; it must transmit feelings accessible to the whole people and satisfy the demands of the great masses living in natural laborious conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer subject-matter rooted in common life and universal feelings over esoteric or class-bound themes; works that require an upper-class background to appreciate are judged unimportant or suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject art that exalts beauty over goodness
rubrics_metrics.description: Art must not put the ideal of beauty first in a way that frees people from moral demands; placing beauty above morality leads to decadence, egotism, and the glorification of vice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge works that justify or celebrate immorality on aesthetic grounds as harmful. Beware aesthetic theories that serve as a cover for immoral action or ideology (e.g., overman/decadent doctrines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid art promoting superstition, patriotism, or sensuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Art which produces or perpetuates ecclesiastical superstition, patriotic intoxication, or inflames sensuality is vitiating and harmful to humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and censure works that reinforce religious/ patriotic dogmas or sexual dissoluteness; examples include liturgical arts that support superstition, triumphal patriotic processions, erotic novels, and sexualized imagery in popular media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: value clearness, simplicity, brevity, compression
rubrics_metrics.description: The desirable technique is clearness, simplicity, and brevity—technical complexity as currently prized is often a deforming, class-bound requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating craft, prioritize clarity and compression of expression over ornate or highly specialized technical virtuosity; simpler peasant art may manifest superior technique in these senses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and accessibility of artistic activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Artistic activity should be accessible to all: elementary schools should teach music and drawing so that gifted people among the masses can become artists; art should not be confined to professional schools alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor social and educational structures that democratize basic artistic skills and allow non-professionals to develop; professional schools that create narrow artisanship are suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist's life-condition: lived experience over secure luxury
rubrics_metrics.description: An artist's productiveness depends on living the common life and experiencing struggle; security of maintenance and luxurious detachment are injurious to true artistic output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess creators by whether they remain engaged in ordinary human life and labor. Artists who live in insulated luxury are likely to produce counterfeit or perverted art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and commerce: drive out dealers
rubrics_metrics.description: Until dealers (art market intermediaries) are driven out, the 'temple of art' will not be a temple; art should not be mediated or determined by commercial dealers alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique systems that let market dealers decide artistic value; prefer direct diffusion to the people and formats that do not privilege dealer-driven tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censure art transmitting divisive or antiquated religious/patriotic feelings
rubrics_metrics.description: Art transmitting feelings flowing from antiquated, worn-out religious teaching or exciting exclusive love of one’s own people (patriotic art), or ecstatic admiration of national heroes, should be considered bad and censured by public opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public appraisal oriented to unity to reject such works; distinguish between genuinely unifying religious art and art that perpetuates sectarian division or chauvinism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraisal by the whole people, not an exclusive class
rubrics_metrics.description: The appraisement of art should devolve to the whole people so that a work must satisfy the demands of the masses to be esteemed good, rather than the tastes of a small rich class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging or programming art, include broad popular standards of taste and the reactions of ordinary people rather than relying solely on elite critical opinion.
